questions.question: What does Three.js sit on top of in the browser?
questions.explanation: Three.js is a high-level abstraction over WebGL, the browser's low-level GPU API. It handles all the shader code, buffer management, and draw calls so you don't have to.

questions.question: Which class creates a rectangular box shape in Three.js?
questions.explanation: BoxGeometry creates a rectangular cuboid. The naming pattern is consistent: SphereGeometry, CylinderGeometry, PlaneGeometry, etc.

questions.question: A Three.js Mesh is made up of which two parts?
questions.explanation: A Mesh = Geometry (the shape / vertices) + Material (how it looks / color / lighting response). Both are required.

questions.question: What is the purpose of requestAnimationFrame in a Three.js animation loop?
options: It schedules the render function to run before each screen repaint, synchronized to the display refresh rate
It saves the current frame as a PNG
questions.explanation: requestAnimationFrame calls your function ~60 times per second, synchronized with the monitor's refresh rate. This produces smooth animation and lets the browser pause it when the tab is hidden.

questions.question: Which material type ignores all lights in the scene and always displays its full color?
questions.explanation: MeshBasicMaterial is unlit — it renders flat color regardless of lights. MeshStandardMaterial, MeshPhongMaterial, and MeshLambertMaterial all require lights to be visible.

questions.question: What file format does GLTFLoader load, and why is it preferred for the web?
options: .fbx — because Autodesk tools export it natively
.obj — because it is plain text and easy to parse
.glb — because it is a compact binary format with textures embedded, designed for efficient web delivery
questions.explanation: GLB is the binary form of GLTF. It embeds meshes, textures, and animations into a single file, making it fast to download and parse. GLTF is the open standard for 3D on the web.
